name: Claude Portfolio

targets.name: Merck & Co.
targets.thesis: Low-valuation large pharma with strong 12-month momentum (+67%), trading about 15% above its 200-day average; it adds defensive Health Care exposure.
targets.risks: Pressure on Keytruda's patent cliff or a pipeline setback in the earnings update.

targets.name: Targa Resources
targets.thesis: Fee-based midstream company at a new 52-week high, with low volatility and steady volume growth from the Permian.
targets.risks: A drop in Permian activity or a broad energy selloff.

targets.name: Nucor
targets.thesis: Leading US steelmaker with tariff protection and strong 12-month momentum, trading above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: Steel prices rolling over as industrial demand slows.

targets.name: CrowdStrike
targets.thesis: Leader in endpoint and cloud security; it confirmed its strength this week with a 13% rebound and is well above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: A rich valuation leaves no room for a disappointing quarter.

targets.name: Marathon Petroleum
targets.thesis: Best-in-class refiner benefiting from wide crack spreads and large buybacks; +17% over one month.
targets.risks: Refining margins normalizing after the third-quarter report.

targets.name: Fortinet
targets.thesis: Profitable security vendor whose firewall refresh cycle is under way; strong 12-month momentum and well above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: Firewall demand being pulled forward, which would lead to slower billings.

targets.name: DuPont
targets.thesis: Simplified DuPont after its spinoff, with low volatility and a strong trend; electronics and water units give it quality exposure.
targets.risks: Weak industrial demand hitting its guidance.

targets.name: NetApp
targets.thesis: Storage company benefiting from AI data infrastructure at a reasonable valuation; it is holding up while its hardware peers sell off.
targets.risks: The AI hardware selloff spreading to its shares.

targets.name: Valero Energy
targets.thesis: Low-cost refiner with high cash returns; it diversifies the refining position alongside Marathon.
targets.risks: Margin normalization and too much combined energy exposure.

targets.name: Illumina, Inc.
targets.thesis: Sequencing leader in a sharp turnaround (+171% over 12 months) as demand and margins recover.
targets.risks: High volatility and possible China or competitive setbacks.

targets.name: Viatris
targets.thesis: Cheap generic-drug maker near its 52-week high, with steady cash flow and a defensive profile.
targets.risks: Generic price erosion or regulatory problems at its plants.

targets.name: Keysight Technologies
targets.thesis: Test and measurement leader with exposure to AI networking, 6G and defense; its 12-month trend is still strong.
targets.risks: It is on its 200-day average and moving with the falling AI hardware complex; I would sell if it breaks down further.

targets.name: Morgan Stanley
targets.thesis: High-quality wealth management franchise supported by capital-markets activity; it is a small position to diversify into Financials.
targets.risks: It is the weakest holding and below its 200-day average; first in line to be sold if it keeps lagging.

fill_rule: the Interactive Brokers demo account's fills at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday, 16:00 New York); if the broker cannot be reached, simulated at that day's Lang & Schwarz session end, mid +/- 0.05%
rules: Paper money: $100,000 at the start, in US dollars.
Only S&P 500 companies; 10 to 15 of them.
At most 10% in one company, at least 3% in each one held; cash up to 20%.
At most 3 companies in or out per decision.
Claude decides twice a week: Wednesday evening and Saturday morning.
Orders go to an Interactive Brokers demo account and fill at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday); the site records those fills: same shares, same prices.
Whole shares only, as at the broker.
Interactive Brokers' commission on each order ($1 when a fill has to be simulated); results shown before tax and after a 26% tax if sold.
No short selling, no leverage, no options, no crypto.
